newsitem.title: USA: Ed. Alternatives sees more proceeds in '97.
newsitem.headline: Ed. Alternatives sees more proceeds in '97.

text.p: Education Alternatives Inc, which reported a fiscal 1997 second quarter profit after some non-recurring income from a settlement with its investment manager, said Thursday it expects to record additional proceeds from the settlement during the balance of the year.

Results for its fiscal second quarter and first half ended December 31, 1996, include settlement proceeds of $313,000 and $938,000, respectively, received from the company's investment management firm. The firm agreed to pay Education Alternatives $1.25 million to resolve all remaining issues relating to the firm's management of the company's investment portfolio.
The remaining settlement proceeds of $312,000 will be recorded in income during fiscal 1997 when they are received, the company said in a statement.

Earlier today, Education Alternatives reported earnings for its fiscal 1997 second quarter ended December 31, 1996 of $277,000 or $0.04 a share compared with a net loss of $4.7 million or $0.62 a share a year ago. Revenues for the three months were $1.5 million compared with $74.9 million in the second quarter a year ago.
Revenue for the current year consists primarily of tuition from the company's two private schools.

Prior year results included revenues and expenses associated with two Baltimore, Md. and Hartford, Conn. school management and consulting contracts. These public school contracts were canceled during the third quarter of fiscal 1996 and had no impact on the company's results for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
Education Alternatives shares closed up 1/8 to 5-1/8.
